keyTerms.definition: Splitting heads and MLP matrices across ranks. It needs one all-reduce per sublayer to sum partial outputs.
Splitting layers across stages. Microbatches flow through with point-to-point activation and grad transfers.
(p-1)/(m+p-1). Idle time from fill and drain, shrunk by more microbatches or fewer stages.
One forward, one backward. The schedule keeps the pipeline full and limits in-flight activations to about p microbatches.
tp*pp*dp = N. TP innermost on fast links, PP next, DP outermost.
Storing only layer inputs and recomputing the rest in backward. It multiplies the affordable microbatch count.

recall.question: What are the three levers on the pipeline bubble?
recall.answer: More microbatches m, fewer stages p, and better schedules like 1F1B or interleaved.

recall.question: Why does TP belong innermost in a hybrid layout?
recall.answer: TP communicates per layer with many small all-reduces, so it needs the fastest links. PP uses point-to-point across nodes, DP all-reduces grads once per step and tolerates slower links.

recall.question: What five checks catch parallelism bugs on paper?
recall.answer: tp*pp*dp = N, tp within node size, per-GPU bytes under HBM, m much larger than p, and shard groups matching reduction groups.
